best_for: Organisations on Microsoft 365, and anyone who needs the Windows or Mac desktop client for meetings and chat.

points.title: Limits belong to the plan
points.text: Microsoft's limits page ties meeting size to the plan: up to 300 people on Business Basic, Standard and Premium and on Teams Essentials, and up to 1,000 on larger plans such as E3 and E5. Meetings are capped at 30 hours.

points.title: Smaller caps elsewhere
points.text: Calls started from a chat are capped at 20 people, and a meeting recording is limited to 4 hours or 1.5 GB.

points.title: Windows requirements
points.text: Windows 10 version 19041 or later, with 4 GB of RAM and 3 GB of disk space. Windows LTSC editions are not supported by the desktop client.

points.title: macOS requirements
points.text: One of the three most recent macOS versions, with 4 GB of RAM and 1.5 GB of disk space.

points.title: No native Linux client
points.text: Linux users get Teams for the web and Teams as a progressive web app. Edge, Chrome and Firefox are supported there, in their latest three versions.

points.title: MSIX packages and zips
points.text: The Windows listing ships MSIX packages and zip bundles for x86, x64 and Arm64, with no standard setup .exe.

points.title: Mac is a universal .pkg
points.text: macOS gets a single universal package that runs on both Intel and Apple Silicon.
